english.title: Aid abet counsel and procure common assault
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), aided, abetted, counselled and procured **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) to assault another person, namely **(.. SPECIFY THE PERSON ASSAULTED..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 39 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 44 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording should not be used where physical contact has occurred - use H4302.
(ii) Practical Considerations - a brief resume, for a detailed explanation click on the appropriate links:
Assault is an intentional or reckless act causing the victim to apprehend (fear) immediate and unlawful violence ;
The conduct may take the form of threatening acts, words, gestures or a combination of any two or all three;
The assailant must have the ability to carry out any threat at the time;
No application of force is necessary;
Where there is no force used, question whether the circumstances justify a charge at all (there are very few circumstances - seek CPS advice if possible). If they do, consider first section 5, section 4(1 ) or section 4A of the Public Order Act 1986.
(iii) This offence wording is for common assault by putting in fear of immediate violence and offence wording H4302 is for assault by beating (battery) i.e. where physical contact actually occurs. See DPP v Taylor, DPP v Little (1992) 95 Crim App R 28.
(iv) See the charging standards relative to this charge heading.
(v) This is a summary offence only but see Sections 40 and 41 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
